title: Tuning, Tab and Chord Diagrams
intro: Standard tuning sets the six strings to E A D G B E, from low to high. Guitar music is usually written as tablature or chord diagrams rather than staff notation, because the same pitch can be played in several places on the neck.

blocks.text: From the lowest (thickest, string 6) to the highest (string 1): E2, A2, D3, G3, B3, E4. Adjacent strings are a perfect fourth apart, except G–B, which is a major third. Guitar music is written an octave higher than it sounds, so the low E appears below the treble staff rather than in bass clef.

Why the major third? With fourths all the way, the top string would be F, and a full six-string open chord would not be playable. The G–B third makes the two outer strings both E, two octaves apart, which suits open chords in the common keys (E, A, D, G, C).

items: Tune string 6 (low E) to a reference.
Fret string 6 at the 5th fret: that is A, so tune the open 5th string to match. Do the same up to the G string (5th fret of D = G).
Exception: the B string matches the 4th fret of the G string (because G–B is a major third, four semitones).
Then the open 1st string matches the 5th fret of the B string.
Listen for beats while two strings sound together: as they approach the same pitch the beating slows and stops (see Consonance and Dissonance (#/arts/music-theory/intervals/consonance)).

widget.title: Tuning check: each pair should sound the same

items: Drop D (D A D G B E): lower string 6 a whole step. One-finger power chords on the bottom three strings; much rock and metal.
Open G (D G D G B D): strumming open strings gives G major. Slide guitar and Keith Richards (who also removes string 6).
Open D (D A D F♯ A D) and open E: slide and folk.
DADGAD (D A D G A D): a suspended, drone-like sound; Celtic and modal playing.
Half step down (E♭ A♭ D♭ G♭ B♭ E♭): same shapes, everything a semitone lower; Hendrix, Stevie Ray Vaughan, Van Halen.

blocks.text: A capo clamps across all strings at a fret, moving the nut up. Every chord shape then sounds that many semitones higher: G-shape chords with a capo at fret 2 sound in A. Guitarists use it to keep the open-chord shapes and ringing open strings in any key, and to fit a singer's range.

Tab has six lines, one per string, with the high e string at the top (as if looking down at the neck from above). Numbers on a line are frets to play on that string; 0 is open. Numbers stacked vertically are played together. Standard tab shows pitch and string but usually not rhythm, so it is often printed under staff notation or with rhythm stems.

items: h = hammer-on, p = pull-off, / and \ = slide up and down, b = bend (often with the target: 7b9), r = release, ~ = vibrato, x = muted (dead) note, PM = palm mute.

blocks.text: A chord diagram is a picture of the neck standing upright: vertical lines are strings (low E on the left), horizontal lines frets, dots fingers. An x above a string means do not play it, an o means play it open. Numbers name the fingers (1 index … 4 little finger), and a label like '5fr' gives the starting fret. In text, a diagram is often written as six characters from low to high: C major is x32010.

blocks.title: Capo
blocks.text: A song uses G, C and D shapes with a capo at the 3rd fret. What key does it sound in, and what are the sounding chords?
solution: Each shape is raised 3 semitones: G → B♭, C → E♭, D → F. The song is in B♭ major.

blocks.title: Drop D
blocks.text: In drop D, which notes sound when you barre the bottom three strings at the 5th fret?
solution: Drop D strings 6, 5, 4 are D2, A2, D3. Fret 5 adds 5 semitones: G2, D3, G3. A G power chord (root, fifth, octave).
blocks.answer: G2 D3 G3 (a G5 power chord)

blocks.text: Sources: Denyer, R. (1992). The Guitar Handbook, rev. ed. Knopf; Goodrick, M. (1987). The Advancing Guitarist. Hal Leonard; Hal Leonard (2002). Hal Leonard Guitar Method, Complete Edition (Schmid & Koch). Hal Leonard.
